questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Mauritania about 1,030,700 square kilometres; United Kingdom about 242,495 square kilometres; Guinea-Bissau about 36,125 square kilometres; Luxembourg about 2,593 square kilometres.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Mauritania on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Mauritania on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Nouakchott?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Mauritania is Nouakchott.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Mauritania?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Mauritania article.

questions.proof: The capital city, which is also the biggest city in the country, is Nouakchott.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Mauritania?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Mauritania on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Berber languages” part of the Mauritania article.

questions.proof: In the south Zenaga is spoken and close to the border with Mali in the southeast Tamasheq (a variety of Tuareg) is spoken.
